facts.text: Two world wars were fought at the start of the twentieth century; the League of Nations was established after the First World War and the United Nations after the Second World War.
facts.quote: Two world wars were fought at the start of the twentieth century. ... the League of Nations was established after the First World War and the United Nations was established after the Second World War

facts.text: The League of Nations did not succeed at all; after the use of nuclear weapons in the Second World War, the idea took root that destructive wars should be stopped and that this is the collective responsibility of all nations.
facts.quote: The League of Nations did not succeed at all. But after the use of the nuclear weapons in the Second World War, the idea took root that such destructive wars should be stopped and that it is the collective responsibility of all nations to do so.

facts.text: The Atlantic Treaty was signed between Prime Minister of England Sir Winston Churchill and American President Franklin D Roosevelt during the Second World War on 14 August 1941.
facts.quote: The Atlantic Treaty was signed between Prime Minister of England Sir Winston Churchill and American President Franklin D Roosevelt during the Second World War on 14th August 1941.

facts.text: According to the Atlantic Treaty, a decision was taken to set up a permanent mechanism to establish international security after the Second World War was over.
facts.quote: According to this treaty, a decision was taken to set up a permanent mechanism to establish international security after the Second World War was over.

facts.text: Detailed discussions followed in two conferences among the allied powers in 1944 and 1945, and a draft of the treaty to establish an international organisation was prepared.
facts.quote: Detailed discussions followed on this decision in two conferences among allied powers in 1944 and 1945 and a draft of the treaty to establish an international organisation was prepared.

facts.text: At San Francisco in America, representatives of fifty countries drafted the Charter of the United Nations.
facts.quote: At San Francisco in America, representatives of fifty countries drafted the Charter of the United Nations after discussions.

facts.text: The United Nations was established on 24 October 1945, as soon as the war got over.
facts.quote: As soon as the war got over, the Charter was signed on 24th October 1945 and the United Nations was established.

facts.text: The United Nations is an international organisation of sovereign nations and the world's largest international organisation.
facts.quote: The United Nations is an international organisation of sovereign nations. ... The United Nations is the world's largest international organisation.

facts.text: Objectives of the UN: to establish friendly relations among nations, to enhance international security by solving international disputes, to safeguard and foster human rights and freedom; it also aims at enhancing international economic cooperation.
facts.quote: To establish friendly relations among nations. To enhance international security by solving international disputes. To safeguard and foster human rights and freedom. Along with these, the United Nations also aim at enhancing economic cooperation at the international level.

facts.text: All member countries are bound by duty to respect the diplomatic privileges of sovereign nations, not to attack other countries and to abide by international law and treaties.
facts.quote: All member countries are bound by duty to respect the diplomatic privileges of sovereign nations, not to attack other countries and abide by international law and treaties.

facts.text: Principle 1: all member nations have the same status; there is no discrimination among nations based on geographical size, economic or military power.
facts.quote: All member nations will have the same status. There is no discrimination among nations based on geographical size, economic or military power.

facts.text: Principle 2: all member nations should respect the freedom and geographical unity of other member nations.
facts.quote: All member nations of the United Nations should respect the freedom and geographical unity of other member nations.

facts.text: Principle 3: all member nations should solve their international disputes and mutual differences by peaceful means.
facts.quote: All member nations should solve their international disputes and mutual differences by peaceful means.

facts.text: The UN has six main organs: General Assembly, Security Council, Economic and Social Council, International Court of Justice, Trusteeship Council and Secretariat.
facts.quote: The United Nations has six main organs: (1) General Assembly (2) Security Council (3) Economic and Social Council (4) International Court of Justice (5) Trusteeship Council (6) Secretariat

facts.text: Affiliated organisations of the UN that work in specific areas are called specialised agencies, for example ILO, FAO, WHO, World Bank, IMF, UNICEF and UNESCO.
facts.quote: there are many affiliated organisations of the United Nations that help it in its functions. They are called specialised agencies. ... International Labour Organisation (ILO), Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO), World Health Organisation (WHO), World Bank (WB), International Monetary Fund (IMF), United Nations Children's Fund (UNICEF), United Nations Educational Scientific and Cultural Organisation (UNESCO).

facts.text: All member countries are members of the General Assembly with the same position and status; every year it meets in its session from September to December.
facts.quote: All the member countries are members of the General Assembly. The position and status of all the countries, whether they are rich or poor, big or small, is the same. Every year the General Assembly meets in its session from September to December.

facts.text: The General Assembly discusses issues like environment and disarmament; its decisions are taken by majority in the form of resolutions; it only passes resolutions and does not make laws.
facts.quote: the General Assembly discusses important issues like environment, disarmament, etc. The decisions in the General Assembly are taken by majority. These decisions are in the form of resolutions. Thus, the General Assembly only passes resolutions; it does not make laws.

facts.text: Functions of the General Assembly: to elect the non-permanent members of the Security Council, to choose the Secretary General and the ICJ judges in consultation with the Security Council, and to pass the annual budget of the UN.
facts.quote: (1) To elect the non-permanent members of the Security Council (2) To choose the United Nations Secretary General and the judges of the International Court of Justice (ICJ) in consultation with the Security Council (3) To pass the annual budget of the United Nations

facts.text: The headquarters of the United Nations are at New York; English, French, Russian, Spanish, Chinese and Arabic are its official languages.
facts.quote: The headquarters of the United Nations are at New York. English, French, Russian, Spanish, Chinese and Arabic are the official languages of the United Nations.

facts.text: The Security Council has 15 members: five permanent and ten non-permanent; the non-permanent members are chosen every two years by the General Assembly.
facts.quote: There are 15 members in the Security Council. Of them, five are permanent members, while ten are non-permanent members. The non-permanent members are chosen every two years by the General Assembly.

facts.text: America, Russia, England, France and China are the permanent members of the Security Council and have the veto power.
facts.quote: America, Russia, England, France and China are permanent members of the Security Council. They have the veto power.

facts.text: For any decision, the assent of all five permanent members and four non-permanent members is necessary; if even one permanent member uses the veto (a negative vote), the decision cannot be taken.
facts.quote: For any decision to be taken, the assent of all five permanent members and four non-permanent members is necessary. If even one of the five permanent member uses his veto i.e. gives a negative vote, the decision cannot be taken.

facts.text: The main responsibility of the Security Council is to maintain international peace and security; in a conflict it may resolve the conflict, impose economic sanctions or take a decision of military action against the aggressor nation.
facts.quote: The main responsibility of the Security Council is to maintain international peace and security. ... end / resolve conflict and make efforts to establish peace, impose economic sanctions or take a decision of military action against the aggressor nation.

facts.text: The Security Council also prepares policies for arms control and plays a joint role with the General Assembly in appointing the ICJ judges and the Secretary General.
facts.quote: (2) To prepare policies for arms control (3) To play a joint role along with the General Assembly in the appointments of the judges of the International Court of Justice and of the United Nations Secretary General.

facts.text: The Economic and Social Council coordinates the UN's economic and social policies; it has 54 members selected by the General Assembly, each with a three-year tenure, and one-third are newly chosen each year.
facts.quote: The main objective of this organisation is to coordinate the economic and social policies of the United Nations. The Council has 54 members. They are selected by the General Assembly. Each member has a tenure of three years and each year, one-third of the members are newly chosen.

facts.text: The Economic and Social Council initiates global discussions on poverty, unemployment and economic and social inequality, and coordinates the organisations working with the UN.
facts.quote: Initiate discussions at the global level on issues like poverty, unemployment, economic and social inequality ... Coordinate the functioning of the different organisations working in association with the United Nations.

facts.text: The Secretariat carries out the administrative tasks of the UN; its chief, the Secretary General, is selected by the General Assembly and the Security Council for a tenure of five years.
facts.quote: The Secretariat has the responsibility of carrying out the administrative tasks of the United Nations. The chief of the Secretariat is the Secretary General. He is selected by the General Assembly and the Security Council. His tenure is of five years.

facts.text: Functions of the Secretariat: to call international conferences on problems like climate change, to organise meetings of the General Assembly and Security Council, to compile information and to supply information to the media.
facts.quote: (1) To call international conferences on global problems like climate change, human rights, disarmament, etc. (2) To organise the meetings of the General Assembly and Security Council (3) To compile information (4) To supply information to the media

facts.text: The International Court of Justice is the judicial branch of the UN, located at The Hague in the Netherlands; it has 15 judges chosen by the General Assembly and the Security Council, each with a tenure of nine years.
facts.quote: International Court of Justice means the judicial branch of the United Nations. The International Court of Justice is located at The Hague in the Netherlands. There are 15 judges ... They are chosen by the General Assembly and the Security Council. Every judge has tenure of nine years.

facts.text: Functions of the ICJ: to settle disputes between member nations, to interpret international law authentically and to advise UN organs on legal issues.
facts.quote: (1) To settle the disputes between two or more member nations of the United Nations. (2) To interpret international law authentically. (3) To advise the various organs or subsidiary bodies of the United Nations about legal issues.

facts.text: The International Criminal Court is an inter-governmental organisation and international tribunal with headquarters at The Hague; it can prosecute individuals for genocide, crimes against humanity and war crimes.
facts.quote: The International Criminal Court is an inter-governmental organisation and an international tribunal. Its headquarters are at The Hague in the Netherlands. The International Criminal Court has the jurisdiction to prosecute individuals for international crimes of genocide, crimes against humanity and war crimes

facts.text: After the Second World War, undeveloped territories were placed under the responsibility of developed nations through the Trusteeship Council, to help them develop and establish democracy; its work is over as no trust territories are left.
facts.quote: After the Second World War, the territories that were undeveloped were placed under the responsibility of the developed nations. ... help establish democracy. The work of the Trusteeship Council is over as there are no trust territories left.

facts.text: The work of the Trusteeship Council ended when Palau, an island in the Pacific Ocean east of the Philippines, got independence in 1994.
facts.quote: The work of the Trusteeship Council ended when Palau got independence on 1st November 1994. Palau is an island in the Pacific ocean, 500 m. east of Philippines.

facts.text: UNICEF works towards making nutritious food and health care available to children; several workshops were organised in India on overcoming malnutrition among babies and children.
facts.quote: UNICEF is an affiliated organisation of the United Nations. It works towards making nutritious food and health care available to children. Several workshops were organised in India to find out measures to overcome malnutrition among babies and children.

facts.text: UNESCO works towards peace and security by promoting cooperation between member countries in education, science and culture.
facts.quote: UNESCO, another affiliated organisation of the United Nations works towards peace and security in the world by promoting cooperation between member countries in the fields of education, science and culture.

facts.text: UN member nations came together in 2000 and decided upon the Millennium Development Goals, such as eliminating poverty and hunger, primary education, women's empowerment and fighting diseases like AIDS and malaria; a time period was decided to achieve them.
facts.quote: The United Nations member nations came together in 2000 and decided upon the development goals for the new millennium. ... To eliminate poverty and hunger ... To fight diseases like AIDS, malaria, etc. ... A time period has been decided to achieve these goals.

facts.text: India has made considerable progress towards the Millennium Development Goals with the help of UNICEF and UNESCO.
facts.quote: India has made considerable progress in the direction of achieving the millennium development goals with the help of UNICEF and UNESCO.

facts.text: To settle conflicts peacefully, the UN Charter includes appointing an acceptable intermediary, using the legal procedure, appointing an arbitrator and, if needed, military means.
facts.quote: It includes appointing an intermediary acceptable to the nations involved in the conflict, use the legal procedure, appoint an arbitrator to solve the dispute and if needed, to take recourse to military means

facts.text: In modern times, human security has been threatened by terrorism, racist and religious conflict, so the UN's peace function has acquired importance.
facts.quote: In modern times, human security has been threatened by terrorism, racist and religious conflict. As a result, the function of securing peace of the United Nations has acquired a lot of importance.

facts.text: To restore normalcy in strife-torn areas, the UN starts schools, creates awareness about human rights, makes facilities available and conducts elections.
facts.quote: normalcy is restored as soon as possible by, for example, starting schools, creating awareness among the people about human rights, make social, economic, political facilities available, conduct elections, etc.

facts.text: UN peacekeeping creates circumstances favourable for permanent peace in strife-torn areas; security is provided and help is extended for establishing peace.
facts.quote: The peacekeeping activity of the United Nations involves creating appropriate circumstances favourable for bringing about permanent peace in strife-torn areas. ... In conflict-ridden areas, security is provided and at the same time, help is extended for establishing peace.

facts.text: Actions supplementary to peacekeeping: prevention of conflict and mediation, actually establishing peace, implementing measures of protecting peace, and peace-building.
facts.quote: Prevention of conflict and mediation * Actually establish peace * Implement the measures of protecting peace * Peace-building

facts.text: India participated in the conferences held before the UN was established and brought issues like decolonisation, disarmament and racial segregation to the UN platform.
facts.quote: India had participated in the different Conferences that were held before the establishment of the United Nations. India has participated in bringing issues like decolonisation, disarmament, racial segregation on the United Nations platform.

facts.text: In 1946, India was the first country to raise the question of racism in the United Nations.
facts.quote: In 1946, India was the first country to raise the question of racism in the United Nations.

facts.text: India has always led discussions on the problems of undeveloped and developing countries, has always sent troops to UN peacekeeping forces and has sent an all-woman peacekeeping force as well.
facts.quote: India has always led the discussions about the problems of undeveloped and developing countries. India has always sent her troops to participate in the United Nations peacekeeping forces. Not just that, India has sent an all-woman peacekeeping force as well.
